senses.sense_definition: Relating to one of the classical Greek architectural orders, characterized by sturdy, plain columns without elaborate decoration.

examples.text: The Parthenon is one of the most famous examples of <w>Doric</w> architecture in the world.
The museum entrance features heavy <w>Doric</w> columns that give the building a grand appearance.

senses.sense_definition: Relating to the ancient Greek people known as the Dorians, or to their culture, history, or geographic territory.

examples.text: Historians studied the migration of early <w>Doric</w> tribes into southern Greece.
Several coastal settlements maintained distinctive <w>Doric</w> customs throughout the Hellenistic era.

senses.sense_definition: Relating to the dialect group of Ancient Greek traditionally spoken in parts of southern and western Greece, Crete, and southern Italy.

examples.text: Many choral odes in Greek drama were composed in a conventional <w>Doric</w> dialect.
Scholars discovered inscriptions showing strong <w>Doric</w> linguistic features in western Crete.

senses.sense_definition: Relating to the dialect of Scots spoken in northeastern Scotland, particularly in and around Aberdeenshire.

examples.text: She wrote several poems celebrating the local <w>Doric</w> speech of Aberdeenshire.
Visitors often find the broad <w>Doric</w> accent difficult to understand at first.

senses.sense_definition: Relating to or composed in the Dorian musical mode of ancient Greece.

examples.text: Ancient philosophers believed that music in the <w>Doric</w> mode inspired bravery and self-discipline.
The composer experimented with traditional <w>Doric</w> harmonies to create a somber atmosphere.

senses.sense_definition: The dialect of Lowland Scots spoken natively in the northeast of Scotland, especially around Aberdeen.

examples.text: Her grandfather spoke <w>Doric</w> at home and taught her many regional proverbs.
The local festival celebrates literature and songs performed entirely in <w>Doric</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A group of ancient Greek dialects spoken mainly in western Greece, the Peloponnese, Crete, and parts of southern Italy and Sicily.

examples.text: Spartan citizens communicated in a form of <w>Doric</w> that differed sharply from the Attic spoken in Athens.
Linguists compare early inscriptions in <w>Doric</w> with contemporary texts written in Ionic.
